title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: A TWO-STEP COST SQUEEZE on the exact stack The Construct runs on: Claude Sonnet 5's promotional $2/$10 per-million pricing ends TODAY and standard $3/$15 takes effect tomorrow (a 50% input and input-plus-output increase), and on September 14 the Claude Code weekly limit boost expires for a NET 17% capacity cut — and `September 14`, `promotional pricing` and the 17% figure return ZERO matches across this corpus
bullets.summary: Two separate, independently sourced, dated changes land within fourteen days. First, Sonnet 5's promotional pricing of $2/$10 per million tokens ends August 31, 2026 — today — with standard $3/$15 taking effect September 1. Second, Anthropic's own developer account stated that starting September 14 it is permanently raising standard weekly Claude Code limits by 25% for Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise, and that until then the current temporary 50% increase stays in place. Because the 50% summer boost (running since May 13 and extended three times, most recently through August 31) is being replaced by a permanent 25% bump over the ORIGINAL baseline, today's working capacity falls by roughly 17%: a 100-unit baseline became 150 under the promo and resets to 125 on September 14. This is reported consistently across BleepingComputer, Android Headlines, XenoSpectrum, Startup Fortune and explainX, all tracing to the same ClaudeDevs post, and the framing divergence is itself the story — the announcement says 'raising limits by 25%', the arithmetic against current state says minus 17%.
bullets.how: YES, and this is the most operationally consequential item this scan has surfaced in a fortnight, because unlike the Pentagon ruling or the memory-security literature it has a date, a number, and a bill attached. Both figures are absent from the corpus: `September 14` returns zero matches, `promotional pricing` returns zero, `weekly limit` appears once in seven weeks (07-02), and `17%` appears once in a July file about something else. The Construct runs Hermes, Lens, Mallard, Pulse and the PRAGMA operators continuously against these limits, and this report's own standing open item — six cost levers logged, none pulled, and a single `/cost` call on a long Lens or Pulse session still unmeasured after six days — has now acquired a deadline it did not have yesterday. The honest sequencing is: the price change bites tomorrow and is unavoidable, so nothing to decide there beyond knowing the run rate moves; the capacity change bites in fourteen days and IS actionable, because it is the difference between discovering the cut through a mid-session limit wall and knowing in advance which agents to move to cheaper models. The measurement that was optional last week is now the prerequisite: one `/cost` and `/usage` reading per long-running agent before September 14 establishes the baseline against which a 17% cut can actually be planned for rather than absorbed. Two limits stated plainly. The 17% figure is arithmetic performed by secondary outlets on Anthropic's own numbers, not a number Anthropic published, and it is correct only for users currently saturating the boosted cap — a fleet running well under the limit feels a 25% increase, not a cut, and this report does not know which side of that line The Construct sits on, which is precisely what the unpulled measurement would settle. And the Sonnet 5 price change was carried once, on 08-25, so only the trigger date is new there.

bullets.title: Salesforce and Anthropic announced 'Claudeforce' — Claude embedded in the #1 CRM with Salesforce-in-Claude in pilot now and open beta expected in September — and the product name returns ZERO corpus matches despite `Salesforce` appearing in five prior files
bullets.summary: Salesforce's own newsroom press release, dated August 26, announces Claudeforce, positioned as a partnership putting Claude into Salesforce's CRM surface. The bidirectional half matters more than the headline for this stack: Salesforce IN Claude is available to select pilot customers now and is expected to launch in open beta in September 2026, meaning CRM records become readable and actionable from inside a Claude session rather than only the reverse. Logged from the primary corporate source rather than trade coverage. Stated as a limit: 'expected to launch in open beta in September' is a vendor forward-looking statement, the pilot is select-customer, and no pricing, no tool surface and no MCP details are given in the announcement, so nothing here is buildable this week.
bullets.how: MAYBE, and the interest is structural rather than immediate. `Claudeforce` returns zero matches while `Salesforce` appears in 07-01, 07-18, 08-01, 08-22 and 08-23 — so the vendor was on this scan's radar and the named product was not, which is the same coverage shape flagged repeatedly this week: the category gets tracked, the specific named thing that changes the buying decision does not. For The Construct directly the answer is closer to no — there is no Salesforce tenancy here to connect. For PRAGMA it is a genuine maybe, and the reason is the direction of travel rather than the product: when the CRM of record becomes addressable from inside an agent session, the operator wedge stops being 'we automate around your systems' and becomes 'we operate inside them', and every mid-market client conversation that currently stalls on integration cost gets easier. That is worth watching for the September open beta and worth nothing before it. The disciplined position is to log it, check whether the open beta actually lands in September, and resist the standing temptation of this beat, which is to convert a press release into a strategy slide before the product exists.

bullets.title: MEASURED aggregator lag, not asserted — the official Claude Code changelog was UNREACHABLE from this session today, and the summariser sites that had to be used instead report 2.1.247 (Aug 26) as the latest version when yesterday's run confirmed 2.1.251 (Aug 28) directly from the primary: four versions and five days of drift, quantified
bullets.summary: Today's run could not fetch code.claude.com directly — the fetch was refused because the URL had not appeared in a search result this session, a tooling constraint rather than a site outage — so this entry is explicitly a degraded-confidence reading and is labelled as such. What the searchable aggregators return is the finding: one changelog mirror states the latest version is 2.1.247, published August 26, 2026. Yesterday's run of this same report fetched the canonical changelog directly and recorded 2.1.251 dated August 28, with 2.1.250 (Aug 28) and 2.1.248 (Aug 27) beneath it. A targeted search for 2.1.252 again returns nothing on npm, the GitHub releases page or any changelog tracker, and the features the mirrors describe as recent — gateway spend-limit support in the usage warning, the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN 401 fix, the /model picker height fix — all sit in versions this corpus already carried. No evidence of any Claude Code release in the last 24 hours, and that is stated at the confidence the sources support rather than at the confidence yesterday's primary fetch supported.
bullets.how: MAYBE, and its value is that it converts a recurring hedge into a measurement. This report has said three days running that aggregators drift from the primary; today it can put a number on it — four versions and five days, on the single source this fleet depends on for its own tooling — because yesterday's primary fetch and today's aggregator reading are directly comparable. That is the first quantified estimate of the drift this corpus has ever held, and it was produced by the failure rather than despite it. The operationally useful consequence is a rule the scan should adopt rather than a task anyone must do: when the primary is unreachable, the correct output is the aggregator reading WITH its measured lag attached, not the aggregator reading presented as current, and not silence. Applied honestly today that means: the most recent Claude Code version this report can assert is 2.1.251 from yesterday's primary fetch, the mirrors are five days behind that, and no release in the last 24 hours is a reading rather than a finding. The standing action is untouched and now seven days old — the version check against 2.1.251, no wildcard before a Bash subcommand, no machine setting `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` — and it has now been carried unstarted for a week, which is long enough that it should either be done or dropped from the report.

bullets.title: NULL SWEEP, stated as a result — no frontier flagship, no new MCP server, no AI-agent funding round in the window, and the signage / wayfinding / permitting MCP negative holds for a NINTH consecutive day
bullets.summary: Four categories checked and four nulls, each verified rather than assumed. Frontier models: no release from OpenAI, Google, Meta, Mistral, xAI, DeepSeek or Cohere dated Aug 30-31; the model trackers still show GLM-5.3 Flash (Aug 26) as the most recent, with Gemini 3.7 Flash (Aug 13) and the Aug 5 Meta Muse Spark 1.2 all already carried. MCP: no server released in the window; the newest items a fresh search surfaces are X's Ads MCP server (carried 08-25 and 08-28) and Betterworks v0.74.0 from Aug 13, with the Aug 22 MCP roadmap and Cloudflare's MCP v2 both carried across 08-15 through 08-29. Funding: the only agent-infrastructure round the trackers surface for this period is Sail Research's $80M — which is dated June 25 and was carried on 07-07 — with Baseten's Series F likewise carried; nothing dated Aug 30-31. arXiv: the papers returned on agent architecture and context engineering are 2603.09619, 2510.04618 and 2606.20683, all three of which this corpus carries across 08-24 to 08-27 and 07-11. And a ninth consecutive direct search for a signage, wayfinding or permitting MCP server returned only sign-industry marketing content — ADA renovation guides, NJ permit-cost articles, municipal signage-plan explainers — and no protocol tooling whatsoever.
bullets.how: NO, nothing here changes anything, and it is written down because a null that is checked is different from a null that is assumed. The signage negative is the one worth restating at nine days: the trade Brand 9 actually operates in has no agent-callable surface, nobody is building one, and every search for it returns marketing copy for sign companies. That has now been true for nine consecutive daily checks, which is long enough to stop being an absence and start being a fact about the market — and the corresponding observation is that whoever builds the permitting or wayfinding-spec layer first has no incumbent to displace. This report is not recommending building it; it is recording that the window has stayed open for nine days of looking. On the funding side the useful discipline is that the trackers surfaced Sail Research and Baseten as though current when both are two months old and both are already in this corpus, which is the same lag documented with a number in bullet 3, appearing in a second category on the same day.

praxis_lesson: Today the report's two most useful entries came from the same place: a number attached to something that had only ever been asserted. The cost squeeze is real, dated and quantified - Sonnet 5 goes from $2/$10 to $3/$15 tomorrow and Claude Code's effective weekly capacity falls about 17% on September 14 - and it lands on a fleet whose actual consumption has never been measured, because the single /cost reading this report has recommended for six days remains unpulled. That is the whole lesson in one line: an unmeasured baseline is fine until someone else changes the denominator, and then it is the reason you find out about a 17% cut by hitting a wall mid-session. The second half is the same shape. For three days this scan has said aggregators drift from primary sources; today the primary was unreachable, and that failure produced the first quantified estimate the corpus holds - four versions and five days behind - which is worth more than another day of the unquantified claim. When the primary cannot be reached, publish the secondary reading WITH its measured lag attached rather than presenting it as current or saying nothing, and the same rule applies to the run rate: measure it before the terms change, not after.
